reviews.comment: Professor was nice and did a lot to make sure you succeeded, however, this absolutely is NOT a blow off class. If you think you could be interested in nutrition, don't take it, this class is only for people who know what they are getting into. Very memorization heavy

The notes and lectures helped so much for the exams. They give you a group project that can help bring up your grade if you are struggling. The professor even says at the beginning that this class will be challenging and not an "easy A". Make sure you to create some time to study for the class, the work can catch up to you.

GREAT guy, so passionate about his class. That being said, the exams are hard.... But theyre just like his slides. Don't take his class assuming it's an easy A because you have to work for it. All the exams were online, proctored. It is so lecture heave but the case studies are a guaranteed 100, just study extremely well for the exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy but the way he teaches it makes it interesting to learn by throwing in  jokes in too.  The exams can be tough but with a basic understanding of anatomy, it's easier.
Difficult class but great professor, you have to be ready to work so don't take this if you think it will be a blow-off/ easy-a.
THIS IS NOT A BLOW OFF CLASS. I am not a science major and thought this class would be easy. It is not! I took the online class he did give extra credit opportunities.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course focused on diseases and how nutrition affects bodily systems. I struggled due to the medical content and memorization-heavy material. The instructor offers extra credit, but there are many assignments. Overall, the material is interesting, but the class can be challenging for students who prefer application-based learning.

Super chill guy, he does kahoots before exams to help you see what might be on it. The exams are literally just copy paste from his slides. Its alot of slides, but manageable if you stay on top of it. I would take his class again. Not an easy A, but a gratifying one.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There was a lot of information but at least it's all interesting. There were 4 exams, 7 quizzes, 3 case studies, and a group case. It took effort but hprofessor was available and helpful the 3 time I went to office hours. Really smart guy. He's funny too. He even helped me get a job! And there is a bunch of extra credit.

I'm a junior BIMs major who has taken all the premed prereqs. I knew a lot before taking the class, but you will learn A LOT of medical conditions. I took notes of ALL lecture slides before weekly quizzes and reviewed them before exams. Treat it like an in person class and an A should be easily achievable. Workload equivalent to BIOL 319 lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Campbell is a super nice guy and a good prof. His exams do cover a lot of material, but honestly it is not that hard if you understand his lectures. His lectures were long and covered a lot of material but it was an hour and 15 min class. I would 100% take him for this course.
Great professor, he gives extra credit. He is really entertaining and makes lecture fun! I enjoyed attending class and exams were pretty easy.

Tad was an excellent teacher and an amazing person! He was very organized and always willing to answer any questions. His tests were very straightforward if you actually paid attention and studied, and his review sessions before exams were very helpful. He is also literally so funny and such a nice guy. Take his class!

This class covers so much material on each exam (7 chapters each with 80 slides each chapter) and a comprehensive exam. While the tests are not hard, you do have to study a lot. Attendance is not mandatory and he does give extra credit. His lectures are so boring because he reads from the slides but the exams go over everything on the slides.

I don't know why people rate him so poorly. His tests are very straight forward, a few tricky questions, but not hard to get an A. He's very nice and he gives a lot of extra credit through easy discussions every week. As long as you have self discipline to watch the lectures and take notes, you'll be fine.

Tad is a good prof and is knowledgeable in his field of work. Yes, his lectures can be very long and get a little boring, but the class is very content-heavy, so you can't really blame him. He is a super nice guy and is willing to answer any of your questions. I would definitely take him again.

Based on other reviews, I wasn't sure what to expect, but my experience couldn't have been more different. He was present, knowledgeable, funny, and clearly cared about student success. Exams were on what was covred in lecture, and he met with me several times to help me improve my studying. Not easy,but fair, with lots of extra credit.I have an A.

Be ready to study long and hard. I studied for hours on end, and have taken an a&p and a nutrition class previously and they were both easier to than this class.The exams are super hard and very specific. While an online class, lectures were super long and everything is extremely fast paced. Be prepared to take heavy notes and do a lot of studying.

Do not take this class if you can avoid it. It is not a blow off class AT ALL. I had to fight for my life to get my grade up after failing the first quiz. Lectures each week are over an hour long. Weekly quizzes. Tests are super hard. All lock down and proctored. Prof also sent a passive aggressive email out. Would not recommend. Save yourself.

Lectures were very long and boring. A LOT of memorization, but the material itself was pretty simple. He seems like a funny, sweet guy. One group presentation that's a free A. Exam medians were 81, 86, 87 and 89.

Pick a different BDE, literally anything else... Anytime he would email me a "reminder" it didn't come off very friendly. Some of the lectures were quite lengthy. Be prepared to be asked super specific questions on the exams and you have 10 minute quizzes that are pretty stressful.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this professor if you want a good GPA. We were expected to memorize enough nutrition information to pass for registered dietitians overnight. Despite putting in consistent effort and studying hard, the exams were extremely difficult, disconnected from the lectures, and earning even a C felt impossible.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: YOU HAVE TO PUT IN EFFORT. I was on verge of failing and I needed it this last credit to pass. I was doing bare minimum and missing assignments, but luckily, I talk to him and he worked with me and helped me out a lot, super nice. I believe he curved my grade so he saved me. Be ready to watch lectures and don't expect an “easy credit” like me.

Never available and TA was the main person that replied to students. Changed last minute the grading policy and to pass the class you must memorize a big amount of concepts for exams. This class requires a lot of effort for just being an elective.
This has to be the worst BMIS elective I've ever taken. He is not an understanding prof and isn't very kind.

Never heard from the prof. The TA ran the course. Exams were extremely hard to even get a 70 on. This course was more A&P than nutrition. I felt like i should be a certified dietitian with how much overload was in this course. DO NOT TAKE. This was one of the most exhausting courses I have had and it was an elective. Unless you are required, run.

The TA ran the course, barely heard from actual professor. Exams were wordy and long. Way too strict for an elective. Final project guidelines were ridiculous. Content was interesting but there could have been better ways to keep the course engaging besides purely exams and quizzes.

HE is a ghost. Hardest class ever. Tell me why this class is harder than ochem 1 and AP 1 COMBINED. Exams are devastating, he is not helpful at all. Extra hard exams, drop this class asap (even if you think that you will be fine, no you wont) I only kept an A bacause spent HOURS MEMORIZING CONTENT. Exams are so exacrt and tricky. RUNN AWAY NOW!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I took this class an my life and physical science credit, and this class had the longest lectures and slideshows required to learn, not to mention the weekly quizzes that were brutal. Test Reviews = not helpful at all. TA led the class, Campbell was MIA basically. WORST CLASS EVER! I am very disappointed about this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only thing he was involved in in his own class was lecture recordings. If you think he will help you with anything at all good luck. His exams don't match the guides so unless you memorize every single piece of information from hours upon hours of lecture, you will not be prepared. Interesting content but horrible class.

Can't make an accurate or helpful exam review. Sat on "review" sessions for HOURS.... still didn't have helpful info. TA is nice, I had some issues with my group project (they dropped the class mid project) and she got me into a new group and communicated effectively. However, would not EVER recommend taking, save your sanity- trust.
Quizzes for each unit. Lots of information to learn. Lectures are interesting. Professor is available for office hours. It's not an easy A but I have an A with some work.

Mr. Campbell was a ghost in his own class. I only talked to his GA Tara and she was nice. 2-6 hours of lectures a week for a simple life science class made it hard to focus on my more important classes. Memorization is the whole aspect of this class and if you have trouble doing that good luck! Whole class was covering ALL of nutrition in 18 weeks.

I was given a group project, but my group was impossible to reach. Another professor told me I could complete it alone, so I worked all day on it. The next day, my instructor said we still had to do it as a group. All my work felt wasted, and his email added stress he didn't seem to care about.

looking for a stressless online class? keep looking. keeping an A in here is stressing me out more than keeping my A in ochem 1. have to take lockdown quizzes/exams on one specific day which happens to be my day FULL of classes & work! :D long lectures, niche topics, only TA ever helps with anything. expectations are clear, but you have to work.

The content itself is very interesting but the tests/quizzes are very demanding. The lectures are very information dense. The tests and quizzes are highly detail oriented and will often call back to niche topics only briefly covered in slides and/or lecture videos. This class has consumed all of my time and I would definitely not take it again.

This class consists of watching 1-4 hours worth of lectures a week and then taking a quiz on it. The lectures are interesting, you just have to be very diligent. Quizzes and tests can be a lot of information, but he does not try to trick you. There is little to no resources, and you really never hear from Mr. Campbell himself, its inly ever the TA.

All quizzes and exams are on lockdown browser and closed note. There's so much information on the lectures that it feels like I'm spending more time on this class than the ones for my major. Only 1 group project with mandatory participation for the presentation and there's an extra credit discussion post every week. Would not take his class again.
